rationale: Evidence: all 60 trials ran off track on every development track. Progress was 0.12 on the oval, 0.055 on the s-bend and 0.045 on the slalom, with about 2 line-loss events per run. The off-track limit here is 0.06 m, and max_error sits at about 0.06, so the robot leaves the tape at its first major disturbance. rms_error (0.023 to 0.028) and steering_oscillation (about 0.14) are both low, so the controller is not jittering. The failure is therefore not oscillation. It is the line being lost and the robot then running wide, most likely during fast entry into bends. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.8 to 1.4. Less speed means less slip and centrifugal drift in bends, and it gives the steering time to recover from a line loss. (2) kd 0.1 to 0.3. Extra damping on the change in signal should reduce overshoot as the sensors swing across the edge of the tape. (3) ki 0.1 to 0.05. The integral term is not needed to correct a 2 percent motor mismatch and could wind up during line loss. (4) kp kept at 4.0 for now, so this change isolates the speed and damping effects. Geometry is unchanged so the result can be attributed to the controller. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and longer progress on all three tracks. The main risk is that 1.4 is too slow to finish in 3.0 s. Next measurements: progress and max_error per track, line_loss_events, and completion_time. If the robot now stays on track but progress stalls below 1, raise base_speed toward 2.0. If it still leaves the track in bends with low oscillation, raise kp to about 5.0. If line losses persist at bend entries, test search_right or search_left.
